chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"My father bought land and stipulated with its owner that he would give him silver coins (dirhams), ten dirhams for every dinar."
ai.seo_question: What was the specific currency stipulation in the land sale narrated by the Imam's father?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the permissibility of stipulating specific currency denominations (gold dinars and silver dirhams) in sales contracts, a practice known as *istihqaq al-thaman*. It highlights the flexibility in early Islamic commercial law regarding the medium of exchange, provided the value is fixed and clear, thereby preventing ambiguity (*gharar*) in transactions. This precedent supports the Shia juristic view that parties may agree on the specific type of currency for payment, even if it differs from the standard circulating tender at the time.
